reviews.author: Mike Graham
reviews.text: If I could post minus scores they would certainly get a minus score. I have a serious condition which is causing me excruciating pain. 9 weeks ago I had an appointment with a doctor from this clinic. He promised me that a letter would be sent to the hospital so I could have some scans. Due to no correspondence coming from this surgery other than to fill out surveys from Surveymonkey, I have to call repeatedly. Most times nobody will answer the phone. After no letter being sent I requested an emergency appointment and complained. As soon as I complained I was given an emergency face to face appointment. The doctor and receptionist apologized unreservedly and admitted my care was poor at this clinic. They promised me the letter would be sent as priority that day . Almost two weeks later after another 5 calls to the clinic I am told that the letter still hasn't been sent. Doctor has given me no pain relief and does not know anything about my condition. I cannot go to the hospital as I need a referral from a GP. We wonder why the NHS is in a poor state and underfunded and then look at this clinic and you see your answer. They do not care for you correctly. They allow your condition to deteriorate and do not make the correct referrals to the hospital at the right time . This means that the cost of your care increases massively and the length of time you suffer and the time it takes for you to get well again increases which in turn shortens your life span. They ignore the telephone. The receptionists are rude . They get prescriptions wrong all the time and seems like they alter your prescription without authorisation. The doctors seem to lack knowledge and common sense. The clinic is constantly empty but there are doctors and nurses there and yet they can never give you an appointment. The NHS need to do something regarding this type of doctor service. DO NOT USE THIS CLINIC. Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Thank you for your feedback. reviews.author: John Mccormack
reviews.text: Only recently moved to this general practice and I regret moving at all. I’d prefer the 40 minute drive to my previous GPs over the below woeful experiences the last several weeks. Attached image of a confirmation text from the GPs. Booked the morning off work, arrive to the appointment to be told I’m booked in for September. Today is Friday the 15th August. Not Monday the 15th September. Secondly, advised over the phone to register my daughter for the GPs I’ll need to come physically into the building to scan a QR code that isn’t on the website. Scanned, completed and registered. Popped in to see if this has progressed as we’ve heard nothing - nothing on the system, come in with your child to register her. Another morning off work. Finally, the biggest disaster - I’ve had a kidney stone for several weeks, agonising pain. Hospital discharged me with a scan booked that due to a motorway accident I couldn’t attend (things happen, life…). I ended up back in hospital again with kidney pain and was advised to raise with my GP to rebook a scan, raised via patches and requested “update via telephone” (though I’m not sure why you’d bother given they’ll either just update in patches with no notification to you or text, they don’t honour the requested means of contact). No update for a week, I log into patches to find the request has been cancelled due to “more information required” from the GP. Bear in mind the request outlines a doctor at the hospital has outlined I require a kidney scan and to request this from the GPs. Symptoms = kidney pain likely stones (not confirmed yet as need the scan, could be more malicious!) and noted worsening pain. I raise another patches request and am advised to come in later that week. At this point I’ve no more tramadol a new born baby and I can’t move. I’ve rang the GP to ask for help, they advised ring 111, I ring 111 who advise speak to the GP. 111 ring the GP who advise they can’t see me today, so I end up back in hospital. With agonising pain. Avoid entirely. I’ll be moving myself, my partner and our child to another GPs that doesn’t have such shocking reviews. And I can see why. One gentleman behind the reception counter is genuinely lovely and helpful, one male doctor (with a slight lisp, apologies on the description but credit due where credit is due his expertise and professionalism were exceptional and I don’t know his name!) the rest of the staff that I have encountered should take note of the above as my experiences have been of incompetence, unhelpful, rude, demeaning and frustrated tones over the phone. Almost as though it’s somehow MY fault information isn’t being passed between health care “professionals” via hospital > GP and / or completed forms disappearing into the void. The reception staff (excluding the outlined gentleman above) are the embodiment of “every GP receptionist thinks they are a medical expert”. This practise would be laughable if it wasn’t a case of people’s lives and welfare at stake. More than embarrassing, an utter disgrace. Practice response date: 6 months ago Practice response: Thank you for your feedback. We are sorry to hear you have been unwell and are experiencing issues with some members of staff and the patchs system. Your comments have been passed on to the practice manager. If you would like to discuss your feedback further, please either contact the practice directly and ask to speak to the practice manager or contact our patient services team via gtd.feedback@nhs.net.

reviews.author: Devon Tynan
reviews.text: Shocking GP service. I have been a patient here since being a child, I’m now 24 and only in the last year or 2 has this GP service really gone down hill. My main concern at this GP practice is a fairly new member of reception staff called Farzana, she is extremely rude and unhelpful. I recently rang to review my sons records he had blood tests 6 months prior to this phone call where she told me there was a problem with my sons blood results and I needed to make an appointment with a doctor to discuss these where she offered me an appointment for in 3 weeks time. I went to the GP practice to collect a copy of his blood results so I could see which of his bloods were out of range, when I got there she told me I couldn’t collect my 6 year olds blood results without ID, this is not GP policy you only need ID to collect somebody else’s results if they are over 16. I demanded my sons bloods were reviewed by somebody clinical that day as six months had gone by since the bloods were done. Farzana was extremely argumentative. Another receptionist heard and was helpful and understanding and went and got a nurse to review his bloods. The nurse reassured me and said his bloods had been put as no action by a doctor which was completely different to what Farzana had told me on the phone. Farzana did not apologise for the mistake she had made or the panic and upset she had caused me. A couple of weeks later I had to ring again after my son had been bit by a dog, I asked if she could look if he was up to date with his immunisations so I knew if he was covered for his tetanus vaccine, she told me I would have to wait 2 weeks for a nurse to action this. Here are only 2 examples of how unsafe it is for this woman to work on reception. She makes clinical decisions which I would deem as unsafe and are not within her scope of practice, and overall is a very rude unpleasant person to communicate with. Other than the receptionist, waiting times for appointments are extremely long, the doctor is different every appointment which is unfortunate for patients with long term health problems, also the gp practice appears to no longer be offering blood tests, patients are having to go up to tameside hospital to have their bloods done which can be very time consuming. I have had an ongoing problems with my health since October, each doctor I have seen has given me a different opinion, and I feel I am no closer to a diagnosis. As far as I am aware the NHS is supposed to facilitate informed decision making and involving the patient in their own care something I feel this GP practice does very poorly. I have had to take a lot of time out of work to be treated at the walk in centre due to the lack of care given. I am now unfortunately considering moving GP practice which is a shame as I have been a patient for a long time along with my 3 children and a lot of other extended family members.

Nevertheless, how you answer this question usually results in not receiving the said 'emergency appointment' and you are back to the appointment a week away. I know that the NHS is going downhill and this surgery probably is reflective of this. As a working patient I struggle to gain a good service from this surgery. They explained today that they have over 4000 patients which makes a good service difficult. I do have some understanding and It is fine having all the understanding about figures and data and staff. Ultimately, as a patient i just want a good, effective service that supports me 'the patient' and the reality check is that his is just not happening!

My mum has been suffering a bad chest infection she rang lindley medical practice last week to ask for an appointment to be told she’s no longer registered at this medical practice since August 2023. When asked why she was told they sent forms off last year and received a form back to say she’s gone away. Lies Lies Lies as no letters received here. Now my mum is suffering and is in desperate need of antibiotics as she struggles to breathe. Rang 111 was told an out of hours GP will call back in 2 hours waited 6 hours for the phone to ring only to be told a GP will call within the next 6 hours. Now I have to take the day off work to take her to A&E tomorrow. What a joke my mum has worked all her life paid tax and NI contributions and for what this absolute horrific service. Since the pandemic happened its almost impossible to get face to face for my young baby too, it takes 3 to 4 days of phoning at 8am to even get a phone appointment. After 3 telephone appointments for my under 1 year old In the last 3 weeks I asked for a face to face app today because my baby is not getting better.GP said I can bring baby in within an hour, I tried to explain I need alittle longer but GP didn’t care to hear it she insisted I attend within the hour or baby won’t be seen so I agreed. So when I finally did get a face to face appointment there was 0 flexibility offered which is not good when have other children to get to school. I must say the GP’s and reception staff in general are lovely and GP’s used to be really thorough when seen face to face, but that is unfortunately not the case anymore and the telephone appointments with the GP’s are just pointless and rushed. I will be changing GP, I know the pandemic has put an added pressure on NHS but I can honestly say after 3 years of going from bad to worse Lindley have no excuse for their lack of care & appointments for patients especially the vulnerable elderley patients and young children. I do believe Lindley can return to a really good practice like they once were if patient feedback is taken on board and they actually make changes and manage the practice properly.

reviews.text: Appointment with Dr Zaluki (amazing doctor by the way) on Dec 16th who requested to see me in 4 weeks to review medication. Receptionist was rude and couldn't help, rolled her eyes at colleagues when I insisted I needed the appointment. Eventually was given the earliest available appointment of 3rd February at 11am with Dr Ben Hamida (also a good doctor). This would be a 7 week wait for an appointment, which is appalling but I didn't have much choice (and isn't the first time I've had such a long wait). Arrived today, after taking time out from work as a teacher where my role has to be covered, to be told I had no appointment scheduled. How can this have happened other than if the receptionist on the 16th never booked the appointment in? Also now in a race against time to get repeat medication before my current set runs out. Some decent doctors here if you can get to see them but the practice is terribly run. I will be leaving after today.

reviews.author: Lauren Fisher
reviews.text: I feel this practice is the best example of why the NHS is so stretched and patients have to wait so long for an appointments. They don't seem to follow a good system therefore so many appointments are getting wasted and putting unnecessary pressure on the NHS. I was unable to get an appointment and due to my symptoms was advised to go A&E who done tests and referred me back to my GP for 2 further tests, which were clearly requested on the form so should have been able to book in directly with the nurse for these. The practice couldn't do this, said i needed a routine app with the gp to decide (5 weeks wait) then be referred back to the nurse (within the next 7 days - so 6 weeks minimum). I couldn't wait this long with lower body numbness so visited the walk in (2nd app in NHS) referred for bloods as A&E had advised. I attended the bloods appointment (3rd appointment in NHS) where they were unable to take said bloods which had now been documented as required twice. I was then advised i needed to see another GP to be referred back to the nurse - if I had stayed with this practice that would be 5 appointments, 5 mornings off work (self employed dental therapist so cancelling NHS patients of my own). I registered at a practice on Tuesday and have had my new patient check and the bloods that were requested by A&E within 2 days. Thee nurse at my new practice read the discharge note from A&E and done bloods as it was clearly stated by the Doctor that it was required. Please look into the way you run your practice, I totally understand practice protocols as i have managed a dental practice myself and worked in a GP surgery. The way you operate is ineffective and is straining the NHS therefore inconveniencing your patients. On a positive note i feel all the staff i have met in the short time at the practice have been very nice, pleasent and do try to help there just bound by the lack of appointments of protocols they have to follow

reviews.author: M. Jones
reviews.text: One gp here was nice because he listened to me when I had problems with my mental health. But the other GP (the arrogant and overpowering one) just re-traumatised me when they made me talk through a horrific assault I'd experienced in another healthcare building from a professional. At the time I should have said no to talking through this trauma, but at this time I was so weak because of the PTSD I wasn't putting my own wellbeing first. I got copies of my medical records years later and discovered that this GP didn't type into my records the details of the trauma I had told them of. So that GP had me talking through this trauma (which worsened my mental health and exhausted me) for nothing. Also , it meant that there was less evidence in my medical records. (I was traumatised for years, the NHS minimised this trauma, so did GMC, and I reported too but they failed to act. You're not safe anywhere, and supposedly safe buildings are ideal for predators to work in. Avoid going into appointments on your own if you need something doing. I can't go near most of them now for fear, and many talk down to us anyway while dismissing patients.) This GP also likes to pressure patients ignoring the fact they are fragile, and is the competitive type. Astonishing that they don't understand PTSD and that you can easily worsen the patient's mental health if you are verbally thoughtless. Another thing about this surgery is that the GP's here are not very knowledgeable... I was going in to this surgery coughing non-stop, and they didn't even explore what could have been causing my cough. Well over two years later an open minded respiratory consultant sent me to ENT and we finally discovered that I'd been suffering from LPR for over 2 years. This type of reflux isn't very rare and I'm still shocked that the GP's here didn't even think of this. They would just type "coughing day and night" consistently into my records each time I went into this surgery, and I'd then go home after making no progress. At least I stopped buying useless pills they kept pushing me to buy. Aloe Vera juice worked much better to relieve my symptoms. I'm glad I refused pills for anxiety and depression - they are very bad for the body. Sometimes all doctors do is destroy us.

reviews.text: this place needs a 0 star option. I know it's hard to get placements at GP's but for your own sake avoid this place like the plague. I've been dealing with an illness for the past few years, and Corkland road surgery, more specifically it's reception staff have only ever made things ten times worse. They lose prescriptions. They forget to hand in prescriptions. They tell you they've done things that they haven't and then pass the blame on to other members of staff that aren't in on the day that you speak to them. usually I'd feel bad about condemning an entire practice and it's staff, but over the last few years I've dealt with all of them and I'm not exaggerating when i say that every one of the rotating cast of women on reception is rude, dismissive, and completely inept. They can't carry out the most basic of tasks, and they couldn't care less that the people they're serving come to them often in times of desperation and experiencing pain. Maybe it's a bit idealistic to expect everyone who works for the NHS to actually care about patients (and thankfully I've had experiences at other practices that prove this wrong), but you would hope that they'd at least pretend to care as that's what they're paid to do. i've had to complain about them multiple times in the past already but nothing changes, they keep their jobs and they keep making vulnerable people's lives harder. But it gets worse. When you're at your lowest and simply want to get hold of prescriptions you handed in ages ago, that they "forgot to put through" and you go in to see them in person, be prepared for all four of the girls on reception to laugh in your face. I would name and shame as it's gotten to the point where I've had to take most of their names but honestly they're all as bad as each other. This isn't only the worst GP that I've ever experienced, it's the worst service i've ever experienced bar none. the only silver lining is that I only have to look after myself. God forbid that you leave the care of your children or vulnerable loved ones in the hands of these people.

reviews.text: I left this surgery some time ago. Had been a patient for many years. Good doctors ALWAYS left eventually. Never known such a rapid changeover of gp's in a Practice. He then asks the patient for a Diagnosis and what they think should be the treatment plan!! Personally, I found him to be ignorant, arrogant and completely useless. I never had a problem with any of the Reception staff or other doctors though and the Practice owner's father was a brilliant GP, but sadly died then along came his son to fill the void and the Practice, in my opinion took a complete nose-dive and gp's that had been at the Practice for many years started to leave. reviews.text: If I could give less than 1 star I would. I moved to the area recently and joined this practice. After waiting for repeat appointments that never came, I called and was repeatedly told by receptionists that I'd get a call back. At least ten times over 2 months I've been told this. No one has ever got in touch. There's no practice manager to talk to. All they say is someone will call you back... An absolute danger and liability to their patients if I'm honest.

reviews.text: Horrific. Doctor had absolutely no idea what she was doing. She was unable to use the computer software which led to her calling me to her room verbally, while the announcement on screen called for a different person, who then knocked on the door during my appointment. This person was sent away while my appointment was completed, during which she got my file mixed up with the other person and began my midwife referral on the phone, spelling out the other patient's name. We thought she was spelling out the name of another doctor or something but nope! This was only realised by myself and my partner when she proceeded to ask whether my name was Indian origin??? (She'd literally come to the waiting room and asked for me by my very English name.) She proceeded to talk about things from the other patient's medical history because she was on the wrong page! The receptionist had clearly had enough of this "doctor" too as this wasn't the only mess up she'd had to rectify. We learnt nothing from this appointment, no tests (aside from a blood pressure one which showed as being low, to which she looked at my partner and said "make sure she's eating properly") Not even a confirmation of pregnancy... just straight to a midwife referral. This was an absolutely unreal experience and I will be changing surgeries at my soonest possible opportunity.

reviews.author: john Geary
reviews.text: I have been a patient at this practice for a number of years , unfortunately I have to say over the last 12mths the service and professionalism has significantly deteriorated. it is almost impossible to obtain an appointment with out 3 weeks notice if you work in a job where you can not take time off for a GP appointment and have to arrange in your own time . The reception managers attitude to this problem appears to be that its the patients problem and you should take the time off work to fit in with them. . for many years I have been prescribed medications to cover 2 or 3 months supply. However, now I can only get 1 months supply at a time this means I am now paying between £400 and £500 per year extra for prescriptions. Today I have been informed from another GP that I could buy a pre payment certificate for £104 per year that covers all my medications. ??? There is no information available in the surgery about this. Why have they not informed me ?? I believe we need to increase NHS funding and I have no issues with an increase in taxation to help with this as then we all pay more for the fantastic service the NHS provides .but this practice does not seem to want to help its patients and provides a very poor service . That said the girls on reception are excellent in tough circumstances and poor management

reviews.text: Used to be a good surgery. I understand it’s been difficult in the recent years for the staff but something needs to change. You literally can’t get a appointment. Receptionists are mind blowing: once the didn’t tell the nurse I was there so I almost lost my appointment, another time it was a face-to-face appointment and didn’t tell me so I lost my appointment as I was expecting a call. You keep accepting new patients, how about you try to stay on top of the ones you already have? Not normal for people to get appuntamento weeks later, if one is sick they can’t wait 3 bloody weeks! Absolutely a disgrace to medicine and taxpayer money.

reviews.text: Truly awful. Something has to change. Appointments are now all same-day only (except for routine appointments), but you need to ring at 8am for one. When I talk to others at different surgeries, there may be a wait for an appointment, but it's nothing like this. At least they can book one. reviews.author: Danielle Birkett
reviews.text: I had to leave rock healthcare after being a patient for 6 years. They never answer the phones, I find the staff rude and unempathic. I visited 3 times in 3 months - once for blood tests that were requested by a private practitioner for my thyroid, once for a smear test and once for my annual blood tests due to a genetic condition I have that causes an increased risk in cancer. On my third visit of which was the only one related to my genetic condition I was quite bluntly accused of being a hypocondriac. The nurses words were you need to stop letting this genetic condition get to your head and had I even been diagnosed with this condition' I was so disgusted and upset by this comment that I changed GPs immediately. I have been diagnosed and have to have several screenings due to the fact I'm at an 80% risk of cancer and at a young age. I try my best to manage this condition but the one thing I need is a gp surgery who will take me seriously when I have symptoms. The first time I had a bad experience was when I was repeatedly told by a nurse at rock healthcare that I'm far to young to get bowel cancer and it's highly unlikely. I had to argue with her for several minutes that this isn't the case with my gene, she kept pushing her argument when she didn't even know what my condition was when I first walked in. News flash my dad was only 36 and Stephen Sutton was 18 so unfortunately no it doesn't matter that I'm young. Absolute disgrace of a surgery and shows how detrimental private healthcare services are for our NHS. I'm writing this now as I have been trying to call for my husband's results from a stool sample he sent in over a week ago. I have been unable to get through for 1.5hrs now and we know he has an infection as I have the same one from food poisoning. My new gp surgery got my sample a day later than his and I've nearly finished my antibiotics. However he's still waiting due to the complete mess that is rock healthcare. He has now just handed in his forms to change to my gp who also answered the phone within 2mins this morning for me to get a sick note. So unfortunately rock healthcare can't blame 'a sign of the times' as other gp surgery's in bury have got it right.

reviews.author: MaRu
reviews.text: Disgraceful... this is the lightest way to describe this hellish place. From the very beginning, this place and people are only failing. Receptionists are not competent, rude and doing the job of answering machine! They also demanding details about your disease - if not provided (saying it's a privet and not to share publicly) - they're just hanging up the phone! The only thing that patient will hear is "I can't make an appointment, it's only for emergency". And then they're hanging up the call! You're not the ambulance, get a grip! Than doctors... or "doctors"? There is something very wrong if "doctor" being asked for literally anything is saying: "you can google it". Really? While I've miscarriage, "doctor" was extremely offended that I've asked for medical examination and some explanation what is going on with my pregnancy. No compassion, not even simple, human understanding! After all, when I was struggling with huge anxiety and depression - they told me to google how to fix it! Any documentation/records from hospital or specific examination like scans just no existing in patient file. Nobody can say what happened with your privet, confident data! If you say them that it's not ok, that they are rude and incompetent, you may receive a letter with threat that "Mr. doctor" who is in charge of this circus will withdraw you from the patients list! Well, I'll make it easier for you just by changing the surgery. Even swapping to a vet - that will be more reliable and way more competent, definitely more human friendly. Shame! SHAME!

reviews.text: 2 star is too much for the rock these days Such a shame. reviews.text: The service is terrible! You can never make an appointment here at all. They are always booked out for at least a month, which tells me that they have too many patients. Even so they still accept new patients. I do not recommend you join rock healthcare at all. I am currently on hold for 38 minutes and yet no one answered. Why is it so hard to get hold of them. I gave them my OH form to be filled in months ago however, they still haven't dont it. I cant stress how awful this service is.

reviews.author: R G
reviews.text: Absolutely awful practice, by far the worst I've ever experienced; unhelpful, terribly incompetent and rude staff unfortunately. Found their lead GP to be completely arrogant, apathetic and cold in his behaviour and conduct with no care or interest in the welfare and treatment of patients - all the traits you'd expect not to see in a GP. This is exactly the sort of practice that is dragging down the NHS and you should 100% avoid at all costs!

reviews.author: Val Greenhalgh
reviews.text: Recently took my mum for a scan here. She is disabled and I dropped her at the door to sit and wait for me whilst I parked the car. Someone very efficiently came to collect her and escorted her to her scan. I went to the Star suite but was unsure where she was. I needed to find her as she has severe mobility issues so spoke to the receptionist. She very rudely refused to confirm or deny that my mother was being attended to, and would not even say whether I was in the right place. I understand data protection, but gave my mum's name, dob and address and explained I needed to find her to help her walk, but no help at all. The medical staff undertaking the scan were very good but the receptionist was rude, ignorant and had an appalling attitude with zero communication skills and zero customer service. As the receptionist is the first face to be seen on arrival, I suggest you review your recruitment criteria to ensure you employ people who are pleasant, articulate and approachable, rather than ignorant, unpleasant, jobsworths
